body_text: TRANSFERS The lessons Celtic can learn from January transfer process Celtic FC Arne Engels Celtic transfers Joel Mvuka Junior Adamu Martin O'Neill Shaun Maloney SPFL Tomas Cvancara Football Sport By Josh McCafferty Sports Writer Share 0 Comments Celtic's January recruitment sparked lofty concerns. (Image: Shutterstock) This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. As June rolls around, and the dopamine rush of winning the double slowly but surely wears off, attention turns to Celtic's drastic summer overhaul. A permanent manager is not yet in place. Two senior players are about to see their contracts expire, one has just retired, and six loanees are soon returning to their parent clubs. Add to that the uncertainty over the futures of myriad other first-teamers, and you get a daunting mix. Celtic enter this summer's transfer window under pressure. January, along with the past few windows, was mediocre at best. Here, The Celtic Way explains how January recruitment worked at Celtic, and what lessons can be learned going forward. How did the winter window work at Celtic? The sackings of manager Wilfried Nancy and head of football operations Paul Tisdale five days into January ripped up Celtic's plans. Nancy's 3-4-3 system required players with distinct attributes. Julian Araujo was sounded out early in Nancy's reign and was viewed as capable of playing either at right centre-back in his back three or in the right midfield role that Yang often occupied under the Frenchman. Despite Nancy's premature departure, Araujo, before sustaining a season-ending injury in March, was ultimately a success. The same cannot be said for the other four signings Celtic made in January. Because of the change in manager and subsequent shift in system under Martin O'Neill, the recruitment plans Celtic had at the beginning of the month were ripped up. Instead, without much due diligence, work began to strengthen positions in a 4-3-3 that O'Neill thought lacked depth: striker, right-wing, and central defence. At the time, without a head of football operations in situ, the interim manager and his backroom team shared the load of identifying targets. Shaun Maloney, Mark Fotheringham, and Stephen McManus were central to recruitment. They sought potential signings and showed O'Neill clips and videos of their strengths and weaknesses. O'Neill himself would regularly contact agents. Recruitment work was carried out around the clock and the 74-year-old always had the final say. In the end, Celtic signed strikers Tomas Cvancara and Junior Adamu on loan from Bundesliga clubs Borussia Monchengladbach and Freiburg, right-winger Joel Mvuka on loan from Lorient in France, and central defender Benjamin Arthur on loan from Brentford until the end of the season. Tomas Cvancara joined Celtic on loan in the January transfer window. (Image: Mark Runnacles / Shutterstock) The quartet did not see a single second of action in Celtic's five post-split fixtures and the Scottish Cup final. Granted Cvancara suffered a campaign-curtailing groin injury in April, but for the run-in, O'Neill turned to players he trusted. Indeed, his lack of faith in those who were signed in January paints a bleak picture of Celtic's mid-season recruitment. It appeared rushed and players were misprofiled. Shortly after he joined, O'Neill said of Cvancara: "He’s not a target man, believe it or not. He’s not the John Hartson type, or the type when Chris Sutton played alongside Henrik Larsson. He’s quick, he’s agile." Four days later, Cvancara started for Celtic against Hearts at Tynecastle. He contested 12 aerial duels that afternoon, the joint-most of any outfield player on the pitch. Celtic often used the Czech Republic international as a focal point in attack, even though that was not his style. After joining on deadline day, Mvuka amassed just 87 minutes of competitive action. "The most puzzling element was the shift in profile and the apparent lack of groundwork done," a recruitment analyst for an unnamed SPFL side told The Celtic Way at the time of the Norwegian's arrival. "After targeting inverted, in-form, goal-threat wingers like Fares Ghedjemis and Damir Redzic, the club pivoted to a player who, even on his best days at Bodo/Glimt, was more of a traditional touchline winger, one who had only registered five league goals and one assist since leaving the Arctic Circle in 2023." Centre-back Arthur performed amicably when called upon and fitted seamlessly into the team, but Adamu contributed nothing more than a stoppage-time equaliser against Dundee in the Scottish Cup . In two out of his three starts, he was hooked at half-time. What lessons can Celtic learn for the summer transfer window? Several. Elite football clubs do not have their manager and his assistant coaches working directly on recruitment. There is often a wider team responsible for the successful identification of potential signings. As exclusively revealed by The Celtic Way , James Bell-Walker, a former senior international scout with Chelsea, joined the club at the beginning of January. His impact in the winter window was limited, but in recent weeks and months, Bell-Walker and those on the recruitment team have been compiling a list of potential summer targets, and tentative contact has been made with certain players. But Celtic do not yet have a manager in place. Indeed, any players they sign during this window must adequately suit the new coach's style and system. Read more: Celtic were worthy title winners but data points to a summer warning - Alan Morrison Inside Shaun Maloney's key role in Celtic double: Tactics, Fotheringham & Osmand call Jota's latest injury treatment explained and the research that should concern Celtic The club cannot afford to misprofile signings again, particularly given the vast nature of the upcoming squad rebuild. Most, if not all, new additions must be hits. They also need to hit the ground running. In January, Celtic made the mistake of signing numerous players who were not fully up to speed. Cvancara had completed just two full 90s all season before joining. Adamu had only 146 minutes under his belt in the two months prior to his Parkhead switch, with Mvuka making only seven starts for Lorient in the opening half of the campaign. Arthur's last appearance for Brentford that lasted more than 10 minutes came 13 weeks before he headed north. Signing match-sharp players who are up to speed really does make a difference. Summer is slightly different, wherein new additions have a pre-season to gain fitness. That said, it won't help if Celtic acquire players who barely played in the second half of last season. Equally, refusing to open the wallet does no one any favours. It is 273 days since Celtic last spent a transfer fee to sign a player permanently, as they shelled out £5.5 million on Sebastian Tounekti last September. All of their January signings were loans. As of December 31, 2025, the club has £67.4m in cash reserves. Funds are in place to back the new manager, even without the windfall from possible Champions League qualification. You've got to spend money to make money, as shown by the prospective sale of £11m club-record signing Arne Engels this summer. Arne Engels played a key role in Celtic's double success. (Image: Mark Runnacles / Shutterstock) Celtic rejected a bid believed to be in the region of £25m for the midfielder from English Premier League club Nottingham Forest in January. If his acquisition, lofty performances, and subsequent sale for a hefty profit don't show the Celtic hierarchy that investing in quality talent can bear substantial fruit, nothing will. body_text: Celtic manager latest: Martin O’Neill and Robbie Keane set for talks Celtic's hierarchy are open to Martin O'Neill continuing as manager - if he wants to stay but Robbie Keane is someone the club would like to speak to more formally if O'Neill removes himself as a candidate By Anthony Joseph and Geraint Hughes Monday 1 June 2026 22:59, UK Image: Celtic are set to hold talks with Martin O'Neill this week Celtic principal shareholder Dermot Desmond is due to meet with Martin O’Neill and Robbie Keane this week over the managerial vacancy. It is understood Celtic's hierarchy are open to O'Neill continuing as manager, if he wants to stay - and the terms and conditions are mutually acceptable. But, at the very least, they would like him to have some role at the club to offer guidance and support. O'Neill returned to the club in two spells last term - delivering a dramatic domestic double in the last week of the season. Celtic are reportedly already preparing for life without Reo Hatate as they plan to ‘accept’ a bid for the out of favour midfielder in the summer. body_text: Celtic set for talks with Martin O’Neil and Robbie Keane June 2, 2026 Football Freak Celtic , Clubs and Management , News Celtic majority shareholder Dermot Desmond is set to hold talks with Martin O’Neill and Robbie Keane this week over the Hoops vacant managerial position. O’Neill is in the frame after success as the interim Seville 20038967 , CC BY-SA 4.0 , via Wikimedia Commons Veteran boss Martin O’Neill is in the frame to become the permanent Celtic manager after helping the team claim the domestic double last season while acting as an interim head coach. The double included claiming the SPL title on the final day in dramatic fashion by beating title rivals Hearts 3-1 at Parkhead. The Scottish champions also won the FA Cup 3-1 against Dunfermline in a rather more comfortable fashion. ﻿ The club are open to the 74-year-old extending his stay as Hoops boss, but only if the former Leicester boss wishes to take on the role. However, if he doesn’t want to take on the position of head coach, then the club are keen to keep O’Neill at the club in some form. Keane is also set for talks Biser Todorov (User:Biso) from Sofia, Bulgaria , CC BY-SA 2.0 , via Wikimedia Commons The club are also looking to hold formal talks with their former striker, Robbie Keane, about the vacancy. He is believed to have admirers at the club, including Desmond himself. Keane is available after resigning as head coach of Hungarian outfit Ferencvaros earlier this month, after 16 months with the club. The 45-year-old has enjoyed success in his coaching career. He guided Maccabi Tel Aviv to the Israeli Premier League title in 2024, before winning the Hungarian top-flight title with Ferencvaros in 2025. Bellamy rules himself out of the job Other head coaches have been linked with the vacancy, including former Hoops striker Craig Bellamy, who is currently the head coach of the Wales national team. However, the 46-year-old has recently stated that he is more than happy in his current role . He also revealed that he has already turned down opportunities at club level because he loves his current role. One outsider for the job is Portugal boss Roberto Martinez, but the former Everton boss seems unlikely to get the job, as Celtic are keen to have a head coach in place for pre-season in July. With Martinez at the World Cup with Portugal, the timeframe wouldn’t work for the Hoops. body_text: Ulrik Pedersen / NurPhoto Mohamed Saeed Jun 01, 2026 16:56-05:00 Celtic's next manager? Ex-Liverpool striker in talks to replace Martin O'Neill and wants to add former stars to coaching staff Celtic Premiership R. Keane Robbie Keane has emerged as a serious contender for the vacant Celtic job after holding formal talks with the club hierarchy in London. The former Liverpool and Republic of Ireland striker is pitching an ambitious project to the Hoops board as they weigh up a long-term appointment following a turbulent campaign. Keane enters the frame for Parkhead return Keane has met with members of the Celtic board in London to discuss the possibility of taking over at Parkhead, Daily Record reports. The 45-year-old, who enjoyed a productive loan spell at the club during his playing days in 2010, is keen to land the role and has already outlined his vision for the future of the Scottish champions. Celtic are currently navigating a delicate managerial situation as they decide whether to stick with veteran O'Neill or move in a fresh direction. O'Neill returned to steady the ship following the "disastrous" tenure of Wilfried Nancy and successfully guided the club to the league title on the final day of the season, but his long-term future remains subject to upcoming talks. Advertisement Getty Images Sport An ambitious coaching team revealed In a bid to strengthen his candidacy, Keane has pitched a backroom team with deep roots in Scottish football. The proposed staff includes former Celtic captain Scott Brown, current Celtic B team coach Jonny Hayes, and former Aberdeen manager Stephen Glass. Glass, who served as Keane's assistant during their recent stint at Ferencvaros, is seen as a vital link in this potential arrangement. Keane briefly played alongside Brown at Celtic Park, but the connection between Glass and the former Hoops skipper is the driving force behind the proposal. Glass famously convinced Brown to leave Glasgow for a player-coach role at Aberdeen, and the group remains close, with Brown and Hayes recently visiting Keane and Glass in Budapest as part of their UEFA Pro Licence work. Board faces tough decision over O'Neill While Keane is actively pitching his project, the Celtic board must first resolve the situation with O'Neill. The 74-year-old remains a massive favourite with the supporters, having won nine trophies across two spells at the club. The hierarchy will discuss with O’Neill whether or not the double-winning manager would be prepared to stay on for another season. If O'Neill does extend his stay, he is expected to keep Mark Fotheringham and Shaun Maloney as part of his staff. However, Maloney may be moving into a different capacity after reports surfaced that he is "in the mix for a sporting director/director of football role," as Maloney would prefer to "go upstairs" rather than remain on the touchline. ENJOYED THIS STORY? Add GOAL.com as a preferred source on Google to see more of our reporting Getty Images Sport The pressure of the appointment The Celtic board is under significant pressure to get this appointment right following the fallout from the Nancy era. While Keane has built an impressive managerial CV - winning titles in Israel with Maccabi Tel Aviv and the cup in Hungary with Ferencvaros - his potential appointment has met with some "discontent" among sections of the fanbase due to his previous tenure in Israel. Transfer activity at the club has currently hit a standstill while the managerial search reaches its conclusion. The recruitment team has already started to shortlist transfer targets, but they will not go through with any deals until a new coach is in place.
